title: Durability as an index of endurance exercise performance: Methodological considerations
authors: Hunter B, Maunder E, Jones AM, Gallo G, Muniz-Pumares D
population: Endurance athletes (review of durability assessment protocols)
findings: Durability is defined as resilience to deterioration of physiological variables and performance during or following prolonged exercise.
The construction of the fatiguing protocol affects durability profiles: greater relative intensity and duration produce more marked deterioration of baseline measures.
Assessment design should control factors such as nutrition and environmental characteristics so outcomes are repeatable and comparable between athletes or over time within one athlete.
Protocol parameters should follow the research question or applied context and the athlete's training status.
limitations: Narrative methods review; gives no thresholds or benchmark values in the abstract.
implications: When tracking durability from free-living data, compare only sessions with similar duration, relative intensity, temperature and fuelling; tag each long run with these covariates and exclude or adjust non-comparable sessions.
Do not compare a drift or decoupling value from a hot or unfuelled run against one from a cool, fuelled run without correction.

verification.notes: Crossref (online 2025-03-27) and PubMed (Exp Physiol 2025 Nov;110(11):1612-1624) agree; first author Hunter.
